candidates.title: [material] internal/Transition.mjs directory-imports react-transition-group/TransitionGroupContext, breaking Node ESM (regression since 9.1.0)
candidates.reason: Reported defect is type/build/test-only or visual-testing infrastructure, not original user-facing keyboard regression.
candidates.issueBody:
### Steps to reproduce

`@mui/material@9.1.1/internal/Transition.mjs` (new in 9.1.0) contains a **directory import** that Node's native ESM loader cannot resolve:

```js
// node_modules/@mui/material/internal/Transition.mjs
import TransitionGroupContext from 'react-transition-group/TransitionGroupContext';
```

`react-transition-group@4.4.5` has **no `exports` map**, and `react-transition-group/TransitionGroupContext` is a *directory* whose only content is a legacy redirect `package.json` (`main`/`module` only — no `index.js`, no extension). Resolving that subpath requires bundler-style directory resolution, which Node's ESM loader does not perform.

Minimal repro — load the module through Node's ESM loader (any `"type": "module"` context, or a test runner that externalizes `node_modules` to Node ESM, e.g. Vitest):

```sh
node --input-type=module -e "import '@mui/material/internal/Transition.mjs'"
```

We hit it via Vitest 4 (which externalizes `node_modules` to Node's native ESM loader by default). Any test file importing a MUI component whose graph reaches `internal/Transition.mjs` fails **at import time**.

### Current behavior

```
Error: Directory import '.../node_modules/react-transition-group/TransitionGroupContext' is not supported resolving ES modules imported from .../node_modules/@mui/material/internal/Transition.mjs
Did you mean to import "react-transition-group/cjs/TransitionGroupContext.js"?
```

The app's normal Vite dev server and production build are unaffected — Vite's bundler resolver follows the legacy redirect. Only the Node-native-ESM path breaks.

### Expected behavior

MUI's `.mjs` build should not emit directory imports — it should import a concrete, Node-ESM-resolvable file (e.g. `react-transition-group/esm/TransitionGroupContext.js`) rather than the bare directory subpath.

This is a **regression** against the Node-ESM compatibility established in v7.0.0 (#37335, closed):

- **9.0.x**: `internal/Transition.mjs` does not exist; react-transition-group is imported only via the package root (`import { Transition } from 'react-transition-group'`), which resolves cleanly under Node ESM. No error.
- **9.1.0**: the *Custom Transition component support* feature added `internal/Transition.mjs`, which deep-imports the bare `react-transition-group/TransitionGroupContext` subpath. This introduces the directory import.

Related: #48644 (remove `react-transition-group` entirely, on the v10 roadmap) would also resolve this, but a v10-only fix leaves the regression standing across all of v9.

### Workaround

In Vitest/Vite config, inline `@mui/material` so it is routed through Vite's resolver instead of being externalized to Node ESM:

```js
test: { server: { deps: { inline: [/@mui\/material/] } } }
```

This works but increases test transform time, so it is undesirable as a standing fix.

### Context

| Tech | Version |
| --- | --- |
| `@mui/material` | 9.1.1 (also reproduces on 9.1.0; **not** present in 9.0.x) |
| `react-transition-group` | 4.4.5 (transitive, `^4.4.5`) |
| Node | v24.13.1 |
| Vitest | 4.1.9 |

candidates.title: Autocomplete `groupBy` breaks after creating a new option when all existing options are selected (regression in 7.3.11)
candidates.reason: PR48788 closed unmerged; no applicable merged library fix established (batch15).
candidates.issueBody:
### Steps to reproduce

### Current behavior

After upgrading from **@mui/material 7.3.9** to **7.3.11**, `Autocomplete` throws an exception when using:

* `multiple={true}`
* `groupBy`
* dynamically adding a new option
* `filterSelectedOptions`
* all existing options are already selected

The issue occurs when a new option is created (e.g. on Enter or blur) and becomes the only remaining option in the list because all other options are filtered out as selected.

Error:

```txt
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
```

Reason :

[https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/48327/changes](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/pull/48327/changes)


The exception originates from the grouped rendering path inside Autocomplete.

### Expected behavior

When `groupBy` is enabled, newly created options should be processed through the grouping pipeline in the same way as existing options.

The grouped rendering path should receive grouped option objects:

```js
[
  {
    group: 'All',
    options: [...]
  }
]
```

and should not receive raw option objects.

### Actual behavior

After creating a new option, the grouped rendering path receives a raw option:

```js
[
  {
    id: 'asd',
    name: 'asd'
  }
]
```

while still executing logic that assumes grouped data:

```js
if (groupBy) {
  return renderGroup({
    key: option.key,
    group: option.group,
    children: option.options.map(...)
  });
}
```

Since the option is not grouped:

```js
option.options === undefined
```

which causes:

```txt
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
```

### Reproduction conditions

The issue reproduces only when all of the following are true:

* `multiple={true}`
* `groupBy` is provided
* `filterSelectedOptions` is enabled
* all existing options are selected
* a new option is created dynamically

Example flow:

1. Initial options:

```js
[
  { id: 1, name: 'A', is_recent: false },
  { id: 2, name: 'B', is_recent: true }
]
```

2. Select all options.
3. Create a new option:

```js
{
  id: 'asd',
  name: 'asd',
  is_recent: false
}
```

4. Autocomplete crashes.

### Additional observations

* The issue does **not** reproduce when at least one original option remains unselected.
* Removing `groupBy` completely resolves the issue.
* The same application code works correctly in **7.3.9**.
* The issue appears after upgrading to **7.3.11**.
* Debugging indicates that the grouped rendering path is executed while the rendered options array contains raw options instead of grouped options.

### Suspected cause

The issue appears related to grouped option caching/rendering logic introduced around:

```js
const renderedOptions = popupOpen
  ? groupedOptions
  : previousGroupedOptionsRef.current;
```

During the create-option flow, a non-grouped options array seems to be cached or reused, while the grouped rendering path is still executed.






**Search keywords**: Grouping issue, Autocomplete grouping rendering issue.

candidates.issueBody:
**What package within Headless UI are you using?**

> @headlessui/react

**What version of that package are you using?**

> 2.2.0

**What browser are you using?**

> This issue seems to be a regression introduced in v2 and occurs regardless of the browser version.

**Reproduction URL**

- [Original behavior in v1](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/priceless-clarke-tysdgk?workspaceId=ws_MWqX5se1xRWk6BRzxn4PHV)
- [New behavior in v2](https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/radio-headlessui-v1-forked-p2dzwx?workspaceId=ws_MWqX5se1xRWk6BRzxn4PHV)

**Describe your issue**

Hello **headlessui** team,

We are updating `@headlessui/react` in one of our projects from v1 to v2. After running multiple visual tests, we have identified a potential regression regarding the `Radio` component, which is not mentioned in the [official upgrade guide](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui/releases/tag/%40headlessui%2Freact%40v2.0.0). It seems that the default tag for `RadioGroup.Option` component is set to `div` in v1 [radio-group.tsx#380](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui/blob/%40headlessui/react%40v1.7.19/packages/%40headlessui-react/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.tsx#L380) whereas in v2 the same component which was renamed to `Radio` defines `span` as default tag [radio-group.tsx#468](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui/blob/%40headlessui/react%40v2.2.0/packages/%40headlessui-react/src/components/radio-group/radio-group.tsx#L468).

Given the fact that the library `Deprecated RadioGroup.Option component`

> We've deprecated the RadioGroup.Option in favor of the more terse Radio component.

we would expect the behavior to be consistent. If this is the intended behavior, we totally understand. However, it does break HTML semantics, since div is a block element and span is an inline element. This difference also affects styling, as not all styles apply equally to block and inline elements. I've attached two reproducible examples above so you can see the behavior in action, simply inspect the HTML tag of the Radio element in the preview to verify.

**Mitigation strategies**

In our case, we'll simply add `as="div"` to the Radio element to render it as a `<div>`, matching the default behavior of `RadioGroup.Option`.

**Potential actions**
1. If this is not the intended behavior, we should consider creating a fix that sets the default tag of the `Radio` element to `div`, aligning it with `RadioGroup.Option`. However, applying this change could potentially break projects that have already migrated to v2 and adjusted their codebases to accommodate the new behavior.
2. It may also be worth updating the "Default element changes" section in the [v2 release changelog](https://github.com/tailwindlabs/headlessui/releases/tag/%40headlessui%2Freact%40v2.0.0) to mention Radio. Alternatively, a note could be added under the "Deprecated RadioGroup.Option component" section to clarify this change.

I'm not sure if this issue has been reported before (I couldn't find anything related on the GitHub Issues page), nor did I see it mentioned in any upgrade guides, but wanted to bring this to your attention. Let me know your input regarding this. I believe we need to communicate it somehow to our user base.

Lastly, a big shoutout to @tomaszczubakTW for bringing this regression to my attention and sparking this investigation!

comments.body:
Hey!

While you can still use the `RadioGroupOption` we do recommend using the `Radio` directly. We use `span` instead of `div` because that's a bit of a better default if you render the radio option next to a label.

The main reason we created a _new_ component is to make these more breaking changes while maintaining the old `RadioGroupOption`.

It also better integrates with these new form components like `Field` and `Fieldset`.

I mentioned in the release notes that we changed the default element 👍

When I upgraded to 2.2.9, our `<Editable>` implementation, which used `onChange` and `onEdit`, broke - every time I typed a character into the field, it would trigger a selection of all the text and type over it. 

### Link to Reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/s/dazzling-babycat-djo67m?file=/src/index.tsx

### Steps to reproduce

When I upgraded to 2.2.9, our `<Editable>` implementation, which used `onChange` and `onEdit`, broke - every time I typed a character into the field, it would trigger a selection of all the text and type over it. 

1. Go to https://codesandbox.io/s/gifted-pond-z7ms0e?file=/src/index.tsx (using @chakra-ui/react@2.2.8). This represents a simplified version of our in-app implementation of `<Editable>` with `onChange` and `onEdit` handlers. 
2. Type characters into the input field. Observe that it works!  
![2 2 8](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/729524/190245984-3404d58f-4a79-4566-9f77-c3527e778578.gif)
3. Now, go to https://codesandbox.io/s/dazzling-babycat-djo67m?file=/src/index.tsx (using @chakra-ui/react@2.2.9). 
4. Type characters into the input field. Observe that they eat themselves. 
![2 2 9](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/729524/190246232-36218d4c-c19d-4d2c-9b07-9c42369a6f5c.gif)

The only difference between these two code sandboxes is the Chakra UI version. 

It's entirely possible, by the way, that we weren't using the handlers properly in our original implementation. I wanted to flag this because we didn't change anything about our code and observed a regression from upgrading our Chakra UI version.

Thank you :)

### Describe the issue

After updating to Bootstrap 5.3.2 we have errors where modals are failing to open due to the query selector failing as invalid 

```
selector-engine.js:41 Uncaught DOMException: Failed to execute 'querySelector' on 'Element': '#j_id22:exampleModal' is not a valid selector.
    at Object.findOne (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@latest/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js:6:8558)
    at Object.getElementFromSelector (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@latest/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js:6:9299)
    at HTMLButtonElement.<anonymous> (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@latest/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js:6:55221)
    at HTMLDocument.n (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@latest/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js:6:4238)
```

The target is like `data-bs-target="#j_id22:exampleModal"`. This is a common auto generated identifier from JSF where `:` is used as a seperator.

This code works in 5.3.1 but fails in 5.3.2

### Reduced test cases

Working in 5.3.1: https://codepen.io/codylerum/details/OJrjvBx

Failing in 5.3.2: https://codepen.io/codylerum/pen/WNLEzKz

### What operating system(s) are you seeing the problem on?

macOS

### What browser(s) are you seeing the problem on?

Chrome

### What version of Bootstrap are you using?

5.3.2

comments.body:
Thanks for reporting this issue @codylerum.
Here's a first quick analysis. I don't have the complete history so I'll make some assumptions.

I tried your example in different Bootstrap versions:
- v5.1.3: didn't work
- v5.2.0: didn't work
- v5.2.1: didn't work
- v5.2.2: didn't work
- v5.2.3: didn't work
- v5.3.0: worked
- v5.3.1: worked
- v5.3.2: doesn't work anymore

So it worked from the following commit https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/commit/fcdfee90b3a181573ad6d7aeb13aa481b11f2ef5 which was a refactoring. The corresponding PR doesn't mention such new support.
The commit just before (ef4e2daa48193463b36fdc297d79c6a002e4ee67) didn't work with this example.

In v5.3.2, we roll-backed a part of this refactoring commit which broke the fact to handle multiple IDs (see https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/commit/9900cf33c0d980353303b0fee381199c9ee89fb8).

Maybe I'm wrong, but without much information, I'd say that it worked during this time (v5.3.0 and v5.3.1) by chance.

If this analysis is correct, we could try to make it work by modifying the `getSelector` and by adding this use case in our unit tests.

Thoughts @twbs/js-review?

_(Putting it in v5.3.3 project for now to not forget it)_

@julien-deramond It looks like previously our code that generated this inserted a `\` before the `:` due to how it worked before with jquery. When we upgraded to 5.3.1 this no longer worked so we removed the `\`

```
button: data-bs-target="#j_idt555\:uploadModal"

modal: id="j_idt555:uploadModal"
```

We need a test for sure and we should see if we could do a workaround. Otherwise, we might need to revert #38989 and cut a new patch release soon.

/CC @GeoSot

Some precisions here after a few other quick tests. Considering the CodePen provided by OP, if we execute a simple `document.querySelector`, here's what happens: As pointed out in https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/39189#issuecomment-1721585409, some characters need to be escaped when we want to call `querySelector`. https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/pull/38989 moved the `parseSelector()` back to where it was to handle the multiple ids. However, removing the `parseSelector()` from the `return` operation doesn't escape the characters anymore in the case of an ID containing special characters, so the final call to `findOne` (which is basically a call to `querySelector()`) fails with `#j_id22:exampleModal` for instance. But putting it back escapes `,` which breaks the handling of multiple IDs (`#hello\,#world` instead of `#hello,#world`). We could probably do a workaround here if we are capable of knowing in which case we are and return either the `selector` or `parseSelector(selector)` in `getSelector()` (something like that). I'll try something next week if nobody finds a solution in between.
Hello guys. Sorry for the delay, I have pushed a possible solution. Any feedback accepted

I have this same issue in a different context. 

In BS 5.3.0, I was able to have a collapse with id "QueueableTasks.Queue". This is desired because it is in reference to CakePHP standard of `[Plugin].[controller]`. 

Example: 
https://codepen.io/umer936-the-looper/pen/wvNJYqQ

I do not want to remove the period if possible.

One thing I wanted to point out is that the selector-engine uses `document.querySelector()`, which treats "." as classes and such. If the expectation is for it to be an id, could using `document.getElementById()` be useful?

@GeoSot said it won't be fixed, because this is a bad practice. See https://github.com/twbs/bootstrap/issues/36813#issuecomment-1195141449. You can use another selector like `[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"]` or as well use your own custom class. The solution below will show you how to fix your issue.

HTML:
```html
<!-- For `[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"]` selector. -->
<button class="btn btn-lg btn-info" title="Label 1" data-bs-toggle="tooltip">Button 1</button>
<button class="btn btn-lg btn-success" title="Label 2" data-bs-toggle="tooltip">Button 2</button>

<!-- For `.toggle-tooltip` selector. -->
<button class="btn btn-lg btn-warning toggle-tooltip" title="Label 3">Button 3</button>
<button class="btn btn-lg btn-danger toggle-tooltip" title="Label 4">Button 4</button>
```

JavaScript:
```js
new bootstrap.Tooltip('body', {
    selector: '[data-bs-toggle="tooltip"], .toggle-tooltip'
});
```

-----

Furthermore, @GeoSot, I suggest adding a note in the documentation of the `selector` option to state that the `title` attribute **MUST NOT** be used as selector.

Thanks @BrokenSourceCode !

Turned out quite easy to fix... just grep the js html templates for `title=` and add a target to use in a selector, `data-bs-tooltip` in my case.

### Describe the bug
Starting with `^2.5.0` version, Shoelace components are not working in an Angular app. The issue is with the way the components are being defined I think.
### To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Install angular CLI : `npm install -g @angular/cli`
2. Create test app : `ng new my-app`
3. Install shoelace : `npm install @shoelace-style/shoelace`
4. Add an entry in angular.json to copy assets : `{ "glob": "**/*", "input": "node_modules/@shoelace-style/shoelace", "output": "/shoelace" }`
5. Add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA to app.module.ts : `schemas: [CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA]`
6.  Add sl-button to app.component.html : `<sl-button>Button</sl-button>`

### Demo

Created a codesandbox for the issue : [codesandbox](https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/shoelace-angular-issue-vm4q8d?file=%2Fpackage.json)

### Browser / OS
 - OS: Mac
 - Browser: Firefox
 - Browser version: 117

### Additional information
I can see that the shoelace.js is dowloading all the chunks for the components, but they are not being defined.
If we bump down the version to 2.4.0, it works fine.

comments.body: Prior to [2.5.0](https://shoelace.style/resources/changelog/#id_2_5_0), Shoelace bundled Lit. We now ships two dists: `/cdn` - Bundles dependencies for CDN use `/dist` - No bundling The new `/cdn` dist is the same as what you were using before, so switching to that may work. As for the issue itself, it looks like the modules aren't loading. They seem to be missing extensions, which sounds like the same problem as #1561. @KonnorRogers Any idea why importing `shoelace.js` would trigger Angular to load extensionless modules? This is one being requested (shows the app, not the module): https://vm4q8d-4200.csb.app/shoelace/dist/components/format-date/format-date Here's what it should be (shows the module): https://vm4q8d-4200.csb.app/shoelace/dist/components/format-date/format-date.js
